scenario: A friendly varicella-zoster virus character having a cosy nap curled up inside a giant cut-away nerve cell - the virus's real trick, latency in a sensory ganglion, told as a bedtime scene rather than as illness. Beside it the two things that actually help a child: a smiling lotion bottle with a big soft cotton pad for soothing the itch, and a cheerful shield wearing a sticking plaster for the vaccination. Deliberately no rash, no blisters, no scratching, no needle and no unhappy face - chickenpox is something many children actually go through, so the page stays cosy and reassuring.

prompt:
A black-and-white CHILDREN'S COLORING BOOK page, square 1:1, 1080x1080, drawn as a FULL-BLEED EDGE-TO-EDGE illustration.

FRAMING - READ THIS FIRST: There is NO page border. Do NOT draw a rectangle, a double rule, a thin outer line, a box, a panel edge, a vignette or any margin band around the drawing. The scene is BIGGER than the square and the square CROPS it: the nerve cell's long tail and its branching arms, and the background elements, must run right off the TOP edge, the BOTTOM edge, the LEFT edge and the RIGHT edge, with white space only where the drawing itself leaves it. The very first pixel row and column on all four sides must be part of the artwork or plain white - never a drawn line.

SCENE: A friendly cartoon VARICELLA-ZOSTER VIRUS character having a cosy nap deep inside a giant cartoon NERVE CELL, shown in simple cut-away view.

The virus character is a chunky round ball with a soft, slightly lumpy outline - not a perfect circle. All the way around its rim sit about twenty SHORT, THICK, BLUNT STUDS, each a small rounded closed bump that is WIDER THAN IT IS LONG and sits directly on the body outline with no stalk, no stem and no neck - like the moulded studs on a toy tractor tyre or the bumps on a rubber ball. Each stud is a closed rounded shape a child can colour in; they must never be thin lines, spikes, pins, rays, spines or anything radiating. Inside the round body, draw one simple inner ring so you can see there is a padded layer, and inside that a chunky many-sided shape (a simple faceted ball outline) holding a loose coil of rounded rope for its genes. The virus has a BIG FRIENDLY SLEEPY FACE: two closed happy sleeping eyes drawn as simple downward curves, cheerful eyebrows, a small contented smile, and one tiny stubby arm hugging a soft blanket that is tucked up under its chin. It is snuggled in a cosy round hollow like a bed.

Around it in the same scene: the NERVE CELL is a big friendly character whose rounded cell body fills much of the picture, with a happy calm face of its own; several thick branching arms (dendrites) reach up and off the TOP edge, and one long thick tail (the axon) runs across and off the RIGHT edge. On the LEFT a large chunky cartoon LOTION BOTTLE with a pump top and a cheerful face tips in from the edge, its base running off the left edge, with three big round outlined drops beside it and a big soft round COTTON PAD next to it - the things that soothe an itch. On the lower RIGHT a large chunky cartoon SHIELD with a happy face and a big sticking plaster across it stands guard - the vaccination. Everything is drawn large, simple and chunky so a child can colour inside every shape.

STYLE - coloring book line art:
- BOLD, THICK, EVEN BLACK OUTLINES on pure WHITE. Every shape fully closed.
- ABSOLUTELY NO shading, NO grey tones, NO hatching, NO stippling, NO cross-hatching, NO gradients, NO colour fill, NO solid black areas anywhere.
- Simple, cheerful, chunky cartoon shapes with generous white space inside them.
- Playful, cosy and reassuring.

STRICTLY FORBIDDEN - the page is rejected if any of these appear:
- ANY rectangle, rounded rectangle, square box outline, picture frame, double rule, panel edge, comic panel, border line, outer margin line, ground-line box or vignette anywhere near the edges of the square. NO frame of any kind.
- ANY decorative STARBURST, comic-style radiating burst, "pow"/impact star, sparkle burst, twinkle burst, sunbeam rays, radiating speed lines, motion lines, snooze/sleep swirls or halo of rays behind, around or under any character. NO radiating lines of any kind anywhere on the page. The virus's studs must stay short, blunt, closed and clearly attached to a solid rim so the character never reads as a burst or a star.
- NO text, letters, numbers, words, captions, labels, signatures or watermarks anywhere - not even "Z" sleep letters.
- NO speech bubble, thought bubble or balloon of any kind (one is added separately afterwards).
- NO skin, no rash, no spots on skin, no blisters, no pustules, no scratching, no sick or crying child, no distressed or angry faces, no tears, no thermometer, no needle, no syringe, no hospital bed.
- NO long spikes, NO tail, NO legs and no more than the one small stubby arm on the virus.
